# SWIG bindings for libcosim — spike

**Status:** experimental spike, 2026-11-19. Branch `spike/swig-bindings-v2`,
on top of `feature/binding-friendly-api` (libcosim changes). Nothing pushed.

- Round 1: SWIG on the unmodified libcosim API.
- Round 2: on top of the first binding-friendly libcosim changes.
- **Round 3** (current): libcosimc feature parity, nanosecond times,
  consistent ownership, CI, a libcosimpy compatibility layer, and Java.
  See [Round 3](#round-3-parity-ownership-ci-compatibility-java) at the end.

**Goal:** check whether all language bindings can be generated by SWIG from
**one** shared interface. See `proposals/language-bindings-facade.md`.

## Result in short

| Language | Route | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Python | SWIG Python backend | ✅ 17 tests (`python/tests/test_spike.py`) |
| Python, libcosimpy API | pure-Python layer on the SWIG module (`python/compat/libcosimpy`) | ✅ libcosimpy's own suite: 51/52 |
| C | SWIG **experimental C backend** (SWIG 4.4.1, pinned) | ✅ smoke test, valgrind-clean; C API drift check |
| Julia | `ccall` on the generated C library, finalizers | ✅ smoke test |
| Java | SWIG Java backend | ✅ smoke test |

All of these run under CTest (`ctest -R swig_`) and in the
`ci-swig-bindings` workflow. **Verified on Linux (GCC) and Windows (MSVC
19.4, Visual Studio 2022): 42/42 tests each** (36 libcosim + 6 binding tests).
See [Round 4](#round-4-windows) for what Windows needed.

**Verdict:** "everything through SWIG" works for Python, C, Julia and Java
from one shared interface. The experimental C backend needs care (exception
handling, overloads, ownership, a `throws` bug), all handled once in
`c/cosim_c.i` and documented in the generated header.

## Layout

```
bindings/swig/
  cosim.i                   shared, language-independent interface (566 lines)
  python/cosim_python.i     Python: time/path typemaps, CosimError, copies (135 lines)
  python/compat/libcosimpy/ libcosimpy-compatible API in pure Python (774 lines)
  c/cosim_c.i               C: typemaps, errors, ownership, header docs (188 lines)
  c/reference/cosim_c_wrap.h  reference C API header (drift check)
  java/cosim_java.i         Java: time/path typemaps, CosimException, copies (109 lines)
  python/tests/, c/smoke_test.c, julia/smoke_test.jl, java/test/  tests
```

Generated output: Python package `libcosim` (`_cosim` + `cosim.py`), C library
`cosim_c` + `cosim_c_wrap.h` (323 functions), Java package `libcosim` +
native library `cosim_java`.

## Building and running

SWIG (pinned 4.4.1) and, for Java, a JDK (zulu-openjdk) come from Conan
behind options that are off by default:

```sh
conan install . -of build/spike -s build_type=Release \
    -o "&:swig_bindings=True" -o "&:swig_java=True" --build=missing
B=build/spike/build/Release
source $B/generators/conanbuild.sh
cmake -S . -B $B -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=$B/generators/conan_toolchain.cmake \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DLIBCOSIM_BUILD_SWIG_BINDINGS=ON -DLIBCOSIM_SWIG_JAVA=ON \
      -DPython3_EXECUTABLE=$(which python3) \
      -DLIBCOSIM_SWIG_LIBCOSIMPY_DIR=/path/to/libcosimpy   # optional
cmake --build $B -j
source $B/generators/conanrun.sh
(cd $B && ctest -R swig_ --output-on-failure)
```

Or as in CI: `LIBCOSIM_RUN_TESTS_ON_CONAN_BUILD=1 conan build . -o "&:swig_bindings=True" -o "&:swig_java=True"`.

After an intended change to the C API, update the reference header with
`cmake --build $B --target update_swig_c_api_reference` and commit it.

## How much adaptation was needed

The libcosim headers were **not** modified. Every adaptation in `cosim.i` is
tagged, so it can be counted and later moved into libcosim (proposal §6):

| Tag | Count | Meaning | Move into libcosim? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[HIDE]` | 38 (74 `%ignore` lines in total) | hides extension-API or binding-hostile declarations | Mostly disappears with the user-API / extension-API header split (§6.6) |
| `[ADAPT]` | 14 | `%extend` / `%inline` replacing a hostile signature | Yes: these are the in-place overloads of §6.1–6.2 |
| `[GLUE]` | 3 | one-call loaders (`load_osp_config`, `load_ssp`) | Yes: §6.3 |
| `[REDECL]` | 2 | opaque base classes (`algorithm`, `observer`, `manipulator`, providers) | Disappears with the header split |

The `[ADAPT]` list matches the proposal's §6 predictions closely: time as
`double`, vector-returning getters instead of `gsl::span` out-parameters, a
result struct instead of three output spans, `std::optional` overloads,
`std::string` instead of `filesystem::path`, plain real-time getters and setters
instead of `std::atomic` structs, typed access to the `optional<variant>` start
value, and a log-level setter instead of inline Boost.Log.

## Findings

### General SWIG gotchas (all solved once in `cosim.i`)

1. **`%ignore` by name also hides `%extend` replacements with the same name**
   (including constructors). Hide by full signature, or ignore by name and
   re-enable the replacement by signature (`%rename("%s") ...(sig)`).
2. **`%extend` bodies and container `%template`s are processed where the class
   is declared.** Helpers, result structs and `%template`s must come *before*
   the `%include` of the class header, or conversions silently do not apply
   (a Python list was rejected as `std::vector<value_reference>`).
3. **`std::uint32_t` / `std::int64_t` are unknown to `stdint.i`**, which only
   declares the global names. Without `namespace std { typedef ::uint32_t
   uint32_t; ... }`, `value_reference` becomes an opaque type.
4. **`int64_t` width is platform-dependent:** SWIG must be told
   `-DSWIGWORDSIZE64` on Linux (where it is `long`), but not on Windows/macOS
   (`long long`). Handled in `CMakeLists.txt`. This will matter in CI.
5. **Default arguments:** ignoring the full signature does *not* hide the
   overloads SWIG generates for defaulted arguments. `compactdefaultargs`
   plus one replacement constructor per class avoids this.
6. **UseSWIG naming:** the Python module needs `OUTPUT_NAME cosim` (UseSWIG adds
   the `_`), and libcosim's global per-configuration output directories must
   be overridden for the module.

### SWIG experimental C backend

1. **No catch-all exception handling by default.** Without a `%exception`
   block, any libcosim exception calls `std::terminate` in the caller.
   Solved in `c/cosim_c.i`; errors become a pending `cosim_SWIG_CException`
   with `code` = `cosim::errc` value.
2. **Overloads are name-mangled from parameter types**, e.g.
   `cosim_fixed_step_algorithm_new_std_chrono_duration_Sl_cosim_detail_clock_rep_...`.
   Renaming does not help when hidden overloads had default arguments. Rule
   adopted: **no overloads in the C API**; constructors with variants become
   factory functions (`cosim_fixed_step_algorithm_create(step, threads)`),
   which matches libcosimc's existing naming.
3. **Upcasts are reinterpret casts.** Passing a `cosim_last_value_observer*` to
   `cosim_execution_add_observer(cosim_observer*)` reinterprets
   `shared_ptr<Derived>*` as `shared_ptr<Base>*`. This works for libcosim's
   single-inheritance hierarchy (valgrind-clean) but is formally undefined
   behaviour, and the manual states only single inheritance is supported. C
   callers must cast explicitly.
4. **Ownership is not visible in the header.** Functions returning objects
   return caller-owned handles (`*_delete`); member getters such as
   `cosim_model_description_variables_get` return *borrowed* pointers; string
   getters return a `strdup`ed `const char*` that the caller must `free()`.
   This needs documentation, or a naming convention enforced through `%newobject`.
5. **Parameter names are lost** (`carg1, carg2, ...`) in the generated header.
6. The backend is marked experimental (SWIG warning 524). The manual also
   lists "enums with a context like class or namespace are broken". libcosim's
   enums are namespace-level, and that worked here, but `-namespace cosim` is
   needed to prefix all C names.

### Julia

Plain `ccall` against `libcosim_c` works without any C++ toolchain coupling.
A real package would generate the `ccall` layer from `cosim_c_wrap.h` with
Clang.jl and add finalizers (ownership, finding C-4), a `check()` after each
call (exceptions), and `Dict` / `Vector` conversions. CxxWrap.jl is not needed
for this route.

### libcosim-side findings (candidates for in-place changes)

1. **Not all errors are `cosim::error`.** XML validation failures and missing
   SSD files throw plain `std::runtime_error` (no `errc` code), while a missing
   SSP archive throws `cosim::error` with code 8. Bindings can only give
   reliable error codes if libcosim is consistent.
2. **`variable_causality` and `variable_variability` are unscoped enums**, so
   bindings export bare names (`libcosim.input`, `libcosim.output`, ...). Make
   them `enum class` (like `variable_type`).
3. **Memory leak in OSP config parsing**, unrelated to the bindings: Xerces
   `DOMLSParser` / `DOMLSOutput` objects created in `osp_config_parser` and
   `extended_model_description` are never released (~960 bytes "definitely
   lost" per `load_osp_config` under valgrind).
4. **Verbose default logging:** libcosim logs at debug level by default, which
   floods script output. Bindings need a log-level setter from the start.

## Not covered yet

- macOS (Linux and Windows are verified).
- Packaging: Python wheels (stable ABI), Maven artifacts, a Julia package
  (Clang.jl-generated layer + JLL binaries), C# (not tried).
- Callbacks from guest languages (user-written slaves/observers).
- In-memory scenarios, functions, building a `system_structure` in code,
  saved state.

## Suggested next steps

1. Run the CI workflow on GitHub once pushing is decided (verified locally on
   Linux and Windows). Upload the Windows SWIG package to a Conan remote, so
   CI does not rebuild SWIG with MSYS2 each time.
2. Decide libcosimc's future (a thin hand-written layer over the new libcosim
   API, or the SWIG C API under its own prefix) and libcosimpy's (the
   compatibility layer as a migration path).
3. Clarify the `add_power_bond` parameter naming (finding 7 of round 3).
4. Packaging, starting with Python wheels.
5. Upstream the libcosim branches (fixes first), release as the next minor.

## Round 2: on top of the binding-friendly API

Branch `feature/binding-friendly-api` (from `master`) contains, as separate
commits that can be cherry-picked:

| Commit | Change | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Fix Xerces memory leaks in OSP config parsing | libcosim-side finding 3 | fix |
| Throw cosim::error with error codes from config parsers | libcosim-side finding 1 | fix (non-breaking) |
| Make variable_causality and variable_variability scoped enums | libcosim-side finding 2 | fix (**breaking**) |
| Add plain-value real-time accessors to execution | replaces real-time `[ADAPT]`s | additive |
| Add vector-returning getters to last_value_observer | replaces getter `[ADAPT]`s | additive |
| Add sample-returning getters to time_series_observer | replaces sample `[ADAPT]`s | additive |
| Add one-call loaders for OSP and SSP executions | replaces all `[GLUE]` | additive |
| Make extension-API overrides private in concrete classes | removes 20 `%ignore`s | **breaking** (minor) |

The bindings were then switched to the native API, and `cosim::filesystem::path`
got a typemap per language (Python: `str` / `os.PathLike`; C: `const char*`),
which removed the remaining path adapters.

### Re-measurement

| | Round 1 | Round 2 |
|---|---|---|
| `[ADAPT]` helpers in `cosim.i` | 13 | **7** |
| `[GLUE]` helpers | 2 loaders | **0** |
| `[HIDE]` tags / `%ignore` lines | 38 / 74 | 36 / **59** |
| `cosim.i` lines | 604 | **444** |
| language files (Python + C) | 122 | 168 |
| Python tests / C / Julia | pass / pass / pass | pass / pass / pass |
| valgrind, C smoke test, definitely lost | 960 B (Xerces) | **0 B** |

All seven additive/fix commits keep the existing C++ API working (except the
deliberate enum change), and the full libcosim test suite (35 tests) passes.

### What remains in `cosim.i`, and why

The 7 remaining adapters all wrap types that are idiomatic C++ but have no
natural C representation. They are reasonable to keep binding-side:

| Adapter | C++ type | Could move? |
|---|---|---|
| `execution::simulate_until(time_point)` | `std::optional<time_point>` | Only with an `optional` typemap family per language |
| `fixed_step_algorithm(step, threads = 0)` | `std::optional<unsigned>` | Same |
| `file_observer(logDir, configPath = "")` | two constructors, `std::optional<config>` | Same |
| `configured_execution::simulators()`, `has_end_time()` | `unordered_map`, `std::optional` | `std::map` would remove half |
| `time_series_samples::times_seconds()` | `std::vector<time_point>` | A container typemap per language |
| `variable_description::start_*()` | `std::optional<std::variant<...>>` | No; this is the right C++ type |
| `set_log_level(log_level)` | inline Boost.Log in `log/simple.hpp` | **Yes**: a Boost-free level setter in libcosim |

The C-only factory functions (`*_create`) for classes with several
constructors also remain, because the C backend cannot express overloads.

**The hide-list and the header split.** The proposal (§6.6) assumed that
splitting the headers into a user-API and an extension-API directory would
remove the hide-list. Categorising the 79 `%ignore`s showed it would not:
`cosim.i` already includes only selected headers, and the entries came from

| Source | `%ignore`s | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Extension-API overrides declared **public** in user-facing classes (`last_value_observer::step_complete`, `fixed_step_algorithm::do_step`, ...) | 20 | **Done:** made private (virtual dispatch through the base class is unaffected) |
| Extension or lower-level members of `execution` (`add_slave`, `add_function`, state export, ...) | 13 | Would need `execution` split into user and extension parts |
| Span-based getter overloads (also provider-interface overrides that C++ users call) | 8 | Keep |
| Lower-level loaders, time helpers, exception internals | 16 | Keep (intentional) |
| Idiomatic C++ (optional, variant, operators, move constructors, ...) | 22 | Keep |

So the directory move was not done; making the overrides private gave the
measurable gain (79 → 59) without moving any files.

### New findings in round 2

1. **Member getters in C are borrowed, and it bites.** With the native
   `configured_execution` struct, `cosim_configured_execution_execution_get()`
   returns a pointer *into* the struct. Calling `cosim_execution_delete()` on it
   (correct for the round-1 helper, which returned a copy) caused a double free.
   The member is now `%immutable`, and the tests document the rule. A real C
   API needs one consistent ownership convention, e.g. only methods (owned
   results) and no public data members in the user API.
2. **Overloads hidden by signature do not cause C name-mangling** when they
   have no default arguments: `cosim_last_value_observer_get_real` and
   `cosim_scenario_manager_load_scenario` keep clean names although the C++
   methods are overloaded. Overloads *with* default arguments still do
   (round-1 finding C-2).
3. **C++20 `u8string()` returns `std::u8string`**: path typemaps need an
   explicit cast to `const char*` to compile under both C++17 and C++20.
4. The scoped-enum fix is visible in Python: `libcosim.input` became
   `libcosim.variable_causality_input`.

## Round 3: parity, ownership, CI, compatibility, Java

### libcosim (branch `feature/binding-friendly-api`)

Further additive commits, each with tests (libcosim suite: 36 tests):

| Commit | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `execution_load_options` for the loaders | start time, worker threads, model resolver, algorithm, parameter set; needed by cosim-cli and libcosimc |
| `add_fmu()` and `execution::get_simulators()` | libcosimc's local slave + slave infos |
| `execution::start_simulation()` / `get_status()` | libcosimc's non-blocking start + status; thread-safe (ThreadSanitizer clean) |
| `cosim/log/level.hpp` | log level without Boost.Log in the interface |

cosim-cli (branch `feature/use-libcosim-loaders` in its repo) uses the
loaders: its run output is byte-identical to before, and an SSP without an
algorithm now gives an error instead of a segmentation fault.

### Bindings

- **Time is int64 nanoseconds** everywhere (as in libcosimc/libcosimpy), with
  `to_nanoseconds()` / `to_seconds()` and `*_seconds()` accessors. Python
  rejects float times with a pointer to `to_nanoseconds()`.
- **libcosimc parity**: `add_fmu`, simulators, start/stop/status, ECCO from
  code (`ecco_algorithm`, `add_power_bond`), log level.
- **Ownership**: every returned object is owned by the caller, in all
  languages. Found on the way: Python had the same borrowed-member problem as
  C (`exe.get_model_description(i).variables` read freed memory).
- **CI and platforms**: SWIG pinned; CTest registration; C API drift check
  against a committed reference header; Windows DLL search for Python;
  workflow for Ubuntu and Windows. Locally verified on Linux.
- **libcosimpy compatibility layer**: libcosimpy's unchanged test suite
  passes 51/52 against it.
- **Java**: works from the shared interface with a 109-line Java file.

### New findings in round 3

1. **SWIG C backend bug**: its default `throws` typemaps (used by
   `std::vector::get()` for `std::out_of_range`) record the error but do not
   return, so the wrapper uses an uninitialised result. Overridden in
   `c/cosim_c.i`.
2. **`%naturalvar` is ignored by the C backend**, also for typedef'd time
   types; struct members use the resolved `std::chrono` type names, so the
   time typemaps are registered for those too. Class-type members need
   explicit `get_<member>()` functions in C.
3. **`cosim_SWIG_CException_msg_get()` returns a borrowed string** (an
   exception to the ownership rules); `cosim_last_error_message()` returns an
   owned copy.
4. **compactdefaultargs** copies default-argument expressions verbatim into
   wrappers outside `namespace cosim` (needs `using cosim::duration;`); Java
   then has no default arguments at all.
5. **libcosimpy is out of sync with libcosimc**: its `CosimErrorCode` lacks
   `SIMULATION_ERROR` (11) and has `ZIP_ERROR = 11` where libcosimc has 12.
   This is the drift problem the proposal addresses, found in practice.
6. **libcosimpy's tests depend on `std::unordered_map` iteration order** in
   libcosimc (`slave_infos()`), which is implementation-defined.
7. **`add_power_bond` naming**: libcosim's parameters are named
   `input_a, output_a, input_b, output_b`, but libcosimc and libcosimpy pass an
   FMU *output* as `input_a`. Either the names or the callers are wrong; to be
   checked against the recent ECCO fixes on master.
8. **ECCO units differ within libcosimpy**: `EccoParams` durations are in
   seconds, everything else in nanoseconds.
9. **Java**: the enumerator `variable_type::boolean` becomes `_boolean`.

## Round 4: Windows

Built and tested natively with MSVC 19.4 (Visual Studio 2022, C++20, Conan
profile `msvc`/`194`), driven from WSL through `cmd.exe`. Result: **42/42
tests pass** (36 libcosim + Python, libcosimpy suite, C, C API drift check,
Julia, Java). The generated C header is identical to the Linux reference.

What it took, in the order found (each a separate commit):

1. **SWIG for Windows is built from source by Conan** (no prebuilt
   `swig/4.4.1` binary for this profile on Conan Center). SWIG's recipe uses
   autotools, so Conan fetches MSYS2, winflexbison and pcre2 as build tools,
   for building `swig.exe` only. Nothing of it is linked or shipped.
2. **Python module import library clashed with libcosim's** (`LNK1149`): with
   `OUTPUT_NAME cosim`, MSVC writes `cosim.lib` next to libcosim's `cosim.lib`.
   Moved to a separate directory.
3. **A libcosim test did not compile with MSVC in C++20 mode**
   (`ecco_algorithm_from_system_structure_test`, from master): streaming
   `path::c_str()`, a `const wchar_t*` on Windows, is a deleted operator since
   C++20. Fixed on `fix/libcosim-api-fixes`.
4. **All executables failed with `0xc0000139`**: `conanfile.py` copied the
   DLLs of *all* dependencies next to the executables, including tool
   requirements; the JDK's older `ucrtbase.dll` shadowed the system's. Now
   only host dependencies are copied.
5. **Python test:** Windows cannot delete files the file observer still has
   open; the test now releases its execution before cleaning up.
6. **Java and Julia could not find `cosim.dll`**: when `java.exe` or
   `julia.exe` loads `cosim_java.dll` / `cosim_c.dll`, Windows does not search
   that DLL's directory for its dependencies. The tests put libcosim's
   directory on `PATH`; packaging must handle this for users.
7. **libcosim could not be loaded into a JVM at all** ("The specified
   procedure could not be found"): libzip's DLL is called `zip.dll`, like the
   JVM's own `zip.dll`, which the JVM loads first; `cosim.dll` was then bound
   to the JVM's module. libzip is now linked statically (it is only used
   internally). This affects any Java binding of libcosim on Windows, not just
   SWIG's. Fixed on `fix/libcosim-api-fixes`.
8. **Julia crashed with heap corruption** (`0xc0000374`): the C API said to
   `free()` returned strings, but on Windows memory must be freed by the C
   runtime that allocated it, and Julia's differs. New `cosim_free_string()`;
   the header rules say to use it.

Findings 2, 4, 6, 7 and 8 would have hit Windows users of libcosim's
bindings in practice; 3, 4 and 7 are libcosim issues independent of SWIG.
